rikav ✞ 2025-12-29 11:14 PM
Alright! Here's a little explanation of how this game is going to go.
Each round/day (in a 24 hour cycle starting this weekend or January 2, 2026 8:00 PM) you will be given a different theme.
Submissions channels will be made for all of you. Here you will submit a fitting song for the theme AND a paragraph (or more) of why you think the song fits the theme.
Your explanation may influence judging as it gives the judges perspective on why you've decided to choose that specific song.
Once you submit your song there is NO GOING BACK (your entry is locked instantly) and you CANNOT USE THAT SONG AGAIN. EVER.
Judges will be critiquing each of the entries how they see fit. Relevance to the theme is the most important factor, but at the end of the day if your song is doodoo ass... it's going to be ranked low.
After all submissions are through, or the deadline has passed, I will announce the rankings from 1st to last.
Until we are at 10 players, every round is a DOUBLE ELIMINATION. This means the bottom TWO players will be eliminated. If someone does not submit a song by the deadline, they are automatically eliminated.
(edited)

# Aching Hearts
10:47 PM
To offer your heart is to open yourself to the potential of failure. Of pain, and longing, and suffering. A feeling many of us have become long familiar with. Heartbreak. It lives in the spaces between words, in the silence after a final note, in the ache that lingers long after the song ends.
10:47 PM
Whether it's the loss of a lover, a family fracture, a friendship gone sour, or a moment that simply broke you in half, give us a track that bleeds a little; one that turns pain into something devastatingly beautiful.

Permahealer 2026-01-02 8:39 AM
A few people have asked about the judging criteria, for me personally i went like: Fits Theme: for the first round the theme was 'first impressions', so i judged partly on how striking (not necessarily how good i thought it was) the intro is, with the rest being on how good of an introduction to the artist that song is, so an intro that will catch your attention, and lead you to keep listening if you enjoy that type of music, and then the rest of the song being a showcase of that artist's style and the techniques they use on their other songs, for this one i also partly listened to their other popular songs to see if they fit more in this category Quality: Here I looked more at how technically impressive a song is, like their instrumental, how well layered it is, how crisp it's played, any special effects they might be using to enhance their music, the production value and that sort of jazz, for me more 'complex' intrumentals and good lyricism rank higher on this category (but I'm not the biggest lyrics person, so i'm obviously biased towards the instrumental) Enjoyability: Self explainatory, just how much i personally enjoyed the song. At a 6 it's a song i wouldn't mind listening if it came up on my autoplay, 5 and under it's a skip, while 7 and over I'd go out of my way to listen occasionally (edited)
8:40 AM
. There's also a 'Judge's favorite' mechanic that i'm not sure if Rikav explained (if he did i didn't pay attention), where each judge also gets to pick their favorite song for that round, and that person gets an extra 0.5 points to their final average rating, if i pick your song as my favorite, I'll be showing it in my notes for you that round, idk what the other judges are going for (edited)

. # Songs Toward the Stars
5:40 PM
In 1977, NASA sent Voyager 1 and Voyager 2 hurtling into the void, each carrying a Golden Record. A time capsule of sound, images, and music meant to speak for all of us long after we're gone. It was humanity's introduction to the galaxy: a mix of greetings, prayers, and unrelenting love for the planet we call home.
5:40 PM
For this round, give us a song worthy of the Voyager Golden Record. A singular message cast into the cosmos, meant to tell the universe exactly what it felt like to be alive on Earth.

MrMonolith 2026-01-04 6:36 PM
Tell you what- if it’s inspiration you’re looking for… The picture posted earlier is one of the Earth. Yes, right there on the right-hand side, less than a pixel in size- a pale blue dot against an infinite void of starless skies and camera noise, shot an unfathomable 3.7 billion miles away from Voyager 1. Astronomer Carl Sagan famously writes: From this distant vantage point, the Earth might not seem of any particular interest. But for us, it's different. Consider again that dot. That's here. That's home. That's us. On it everyone you love, everyone you know, everyone you ever heard of, every human being who ever was, lived out their lives. The aggregate of our joy and suffering, thousands of confident religions, ideologies, and economic doctrines, every hunter and forager, every hero and coward, every creator and destroyer of civilization, every king and peasant, every young couple in love, every mother and father, hopeful child, inventor and explorer, every teacher of morals, every corrupt politician, every “superstar", every "supreme leader", every saint and sinner in the history of our species lived there – on a mote of dust suspended in a sunbeam.
6:36 PM
6:39 PM
The human experience, so inherently fundamental to us, is but a fleeting moment in the universe’s mind-numbing infinity. It’s a bold challenge not to consider our own existence, but that is the situation, isn’t it? What is Earth, anyways? What is “everything you’ve ever known?” to you or your artist? What oratorio sings into the vacuum? You decide.

# > Damn Youngins!
7:49 PM
Long before the algorithm decided what we loved, music found us anyway. You turned up the radio in your early-2000s Volkswagen Beetle convertible and there it was: blaring through the speakers as the summer's next unavoidable hit. Fast-forward twenty years and it’s been quietly relegated to the background, a cultural artifact that the Gen Alpha shitters scroll past, never realizing just how iconic the tune once was.
7:49 PM
For this round, dig up a track that ruled its era but somehow fell through the cracks of time, leaving the younger generation none the wiser.

# > Dream Sequence
9:29 PM
At some point, you stop being aware of your body at all. The music doesn't so much play as it happens to you, lifting you from yourself and setting you adrift somewhere vast and unfamiliar. You're watching yourself from a distance, suspended in a place where time folds in on itself and the impossibility of a form with no flesh persists.
9:29 PM
For this round, give us a song that feels like an out-of-body experience. Something surreal, dreamy, and most of all transcendent. The kind of track that hits so hard it makes you forget who you are.

# > One-Hit Wonderland
10:33 PM
There is no greater antithesis to the SOL than choosing a one-hit wonder- the sort of artists that have only one song of notable fame or quality before forever fading into irrelevance as a footnote in music history. Hits form the decades long past will stay with you for a long time… but the face behind it is less remarkable than you’d think.
10:33 PM

# Played by: @Kaitan [S1 - 11th]

# Defense
9:41 PM

HADAKA NO YUSHA

This is the final song that I will submit for VAUNDY and I think this is perfectly fitting for a farewell song. Idk much about the song lyrically cause tbh I don’t rlly care for the lyrics for international songs, however I think listening to music you can’t understand is just as powerful as you listen purely with emotion behind it. At the very beginning this song is just a simple ballad with a guitar and as time progresses into a beautiful rock ballad, balancing yet grit and the roughness of his tone with a balance of sweet string instruments playing in the background. This song in my opinion is arguably one of his best songs and I think a lot of that purely comes from the emotion he sings with. Without even knowing the topic he sings about you can’t understand just tell that whatever he is singing he means with his whole heart and passion. When I think of this theme, of almost a farewell I feel like this song comes to my mind. Something about it feels like the end of something if that makes sense. I think not only does this feel like the perfect song to wrap up the SOL but also a song to end for VAUNDY. It feels like his last hoorah and he’s pouring his heart and soul into making it right. It incorporates many styles we’ve seen from VAUNDY throughout the competition like his soft quiet side in songs like “odoriko”, his rock side from songs like “CHAINSAW BLOOD”, his brilliant use of strings in “Kiseki” or “Yobigoe” and the raspy emotional tone used in “saikai”. The adrupt ending of this song as well feels so fitting also. Like one where the music is up and at its climax and then just stops, leaving room for the listener to digest the music they heard, like after watching a movie that leaves u hanging at every moment. As for why VAUNDY should win well while I can’t say because he’s done the best overall (he hasn’t). HOWEVER VAUNDY has consistently pushed through and beat MAJOR artists while trying to project lyrical themes using only crappy English translators. Each round VAUNDY scraped by in second to last he sniped out a major artist like Laufey Ado and even Kanye and Radiohead. VAUNDY has taken every disadvantage thrown at him and beat the living hell out of it. And when we had highs they were HIGHS VAUNDY has two wins and a few other consistent high placements from the beginning of the game. So yeah gimme the win pls

# Willard!
9:43 PM
# Played by: @Leah [S1 - 10th]
9:44 PM
# Defense
Truce SOL: Leah's Will Wood Defense
Hello, everyone! This is Leah representing Will Wood, and it's been an absolute honor to compete in this season. I honestly can't believe that I'm sitting here writing what's essentially a finale speech for my first ever SOL. I'll keep my opening thoughts brief; just know that I mean everything I...
9:44 PM
Song Explanation Willard is a deeply touching and guttural song that I think does an excellent job of relating feelings of social isolation to the end of the universe as we know it, as corny as that may sound. The orchestral production straddles the line between atmospheric and theatrical in a very satisfying way, with the instrumental flare at the beginning resembling a rocket launching into space and the outro's decrescendo gradually fading into nothing, much like the final fleeting thoughts of a person losing consciousness. The strings, woodwinds, and chimes all complement each other as much as they do Wood's voice: incredibly well. There are also so many lines that stick out to me, either for their layered wordplay or for their ability to pack a massive punch into a bite-sized moment. “You might seem behind bars, but this cage is inside out” is a brilliant way of expressing that even a caged animal has more freedom than Willard does under the pressure of conformity, and “My friend, you've got a friend in me; let's go and make more enemies” never fails to give me goosebumps. The mention of “Pandora's Skinner box” combines would-be disparate concepts in such a clever way that it just inexplicably clicks, and that's not even mentioning the entire first verse being packed full of animal-themed double entendres. This might not be the most impressive song in the world, but it manages to be both bold and subtle in a way that few other artists can accomplish. I can certainly relate to Willard feeling so abandoned by his own species that he seeks out support from animals rather than people, and there's something oddly comforting about knowing he had his closest friend beside him when it all came to an end. As different as they may have seemed on the surface, they stuck together when it mattered the most, leaving behind a legacy of true camaraderie through adversity in their wake.
